invariants.statement: Knowledge Ledger with Disposable Projections is the governing architecture pattern.
Every surfaced fact identifies its canonical source, source revision, ingestion receipt, and derivation path.
Graph, vector, text, cache, and Second-Brain surfaces are rebuildable and never become sole authority.
Ontology changes are versioned, previewed, reviewed, reversible, and attributable.
Department heads remain accountable while teams and agents retain bounded autonomy.
enforced_by: human owner on every milestone, risk, gate, and task

invariants.statement: Every implementation action resolves to a Mission Control task with evidence and rollback.
Authorization is deny by default and search results are security trimmed before ranking or generation.
Retention, disposition, legal hold, privacy, and residency remain source-aware and policy controlled.
Part 11 controls apply only after Quality and Legal approve intended use and the validated-system boundary.
Duplicate, contradiction, and staleness signals never silently delete or overwrite canonical content.
Every answer or recommendation exposes source links, revision time, confidence, and known conflicts.
Milestones, dependencies, risks, gates, and validation are machine readable and fail closed on drift.
SharePoint is the system of record for Mission Control planning records while Mission Control is workflow authority for execution, routing, and evidence policy.
The mirror-is-boring gate must be met before an ontology, discovery, or other new knowledge plane starts.

Graph permissions and least-privilege connector identities are approved.

phase_zero_gates.title: Portal and Second-Brain repository and runtime inventory

phase_zero_gates.title: Part 11 intended-use and validated-system boundary
done_when: Quality and Legal document which records and signatures are regulated.
Validation, audit-trail review, retention, signature, and record-copy obligations have named owners.

phase_zero_gates.title: Authorization and privacy model
done_when: Identity classes, customer and vendor isolation, department access, agent capabilities, and break-glass paths are approved.
Sensitive-data classes and purpose limitations are mapped to enforceable policies.

phase_zero_gates.title: Knowledge ledger and audit-store deployment decision

Ledger transaction-time and valid-time semantics are approved.

phase_zero_gates.title: Mirror-is-boring entry gate
done_when: Mission Control self-check schema is green and architecture parity passes.
Self-check reports live, fresh data with boringGateMet true; recheck before each new-plane milestone starts.

requirements.statement: Each knowledge object shall declare one canonical system and an authoring return path.
The ledger shall preserve immutable assertion versions with valid time and transaction time.
Graph, vector, full-text, cache, and Second-Brain projections shall be rebuildable from versioned sources.
Every assertion and chunk shall carry source identity, source revision, extraction version, and ingestion receipt.
Administrators shall safely propose, preview, review, publish, deprecate, and roll back ontology changes in the Portal.
Ontology versions shall preserve stable identifiers, labels, synonyms, mappings, owners, and effective dates.
Users shall search lexically and semantically across authorized PLX sources with source filters.
Answers shall display citations, revision time, confidence, derivation, and contradiction state.
The system shall flag exact, near, and semantic duplicate candidates without destructive deduplication.
The system shall flag stale and contradictory content using source-aware rules and owner review.
Connectors and retrieval shall enforce least privilege, deny by default, and preserve source ACL semantics.
Agent, MCP, tool, and skill actions shall use registered identities, versioned capabilities, and auditable invocation.
Data classification, minimization, purpose limitation, residency, and subject-right handling shall be source aware.
Retention, disposition, legal hold, and records declaration shall remain governed by approved source policies.
Regulated records shall support accurate and complete copies, protection, retrieval, and approved retention.
Regulated actions shall create secure, computer-generated, time-stamped audit trails attributable to an authorized actor.
Electronic signatures shall be unique, verified, linked to their records, and display required signature meaning.
verification: DocuSign envelope and record linkage test

requirements.statement: Every milestone, task, risk, and gate shall have a named human accountable owner.
Teams and agents may execute only within approved, revocable, and evidence-producing autonomy bounds.
Connectors shall be idempotent, cursor based, observable, replayable, and independently degradable.
Canonical content shall remain readable when the ledger, Second-Brain, or any projection is unavailable.
Projection versions shall identify ledger watermark, ontology version, model version, and build receipt.
Mission Control execution records shall remain linked to delivery evidence and canonical project artifacts.
Customer and vendor knowledge shall be isolated from other tenants before retrieval and generation.
Source deletions and permission changes shall create tombstones and projection removals without erasing audit history.
Program state shall be schema validated with acyclic dependencies and complete requirement coverage before dispatch.
No ontology, discovery, or other new knowledge plane shall start unless the Mission Control mirror-is-boring gate is currently met.
Quality and Legal shall classify each regulated workflow as a closed or open system and approve the corresponding Part 11 controls.
When required by 21 CFR 11.100(c), the organization shall retain evidence of the FDA electronic-signature certification process and scope.
verification: Quality and Legal certification applicability decision

requirements.statement: Non-biometric electronic signatures shall enforce the approved identification components, signing-session behavior, and genuine-owner controls required by 21 CFR 11.200.

tasks.title: Inventory Microsoft 365, Portal, Second-Brain, DocuSign, and registry estates

tasks.title: Approve Part 11 intended use and validation boundary

tasks.title: Approve authority, privacy, residency, and authorization matrices

tasks.title: Implement bitemporal ledger and immutable ingestion receipts
done_when: Assertions support valid-time and transaction-time queries.
Corrections append closure and supersession events without mutating prior assertion payloads.
Every ingest produces a tamper-evident receipt with source revision and canonical digest.

tasks.title: Implement connector and projection receipt contracts

tasks.title: Connect SharePoint and Microsoft 365 canonical records

tasks.title: Qualify audit trails, record copies, signatures, and training controls

tasks.title: Build graph, vector, and full-text projection pipelines

tasks.title: Implement duplicate, stale, and contradiction detection

tasks.title: Build explainable, security-trimmed discovery experience

tasks.title: Enforce Agent Registry, MCP, tool, and skill autonomy bounds

risks.title: Microsoft 365 estate or licensing assumptions are wrong
risks.mitigation: Keep connector and Purview design blocked until tenant, site, region, license, role, and Graph permission evidence is approved.
risks.trigger: Any required feature, site, or permission cannot be demonstrated in the target tenant.

risks.title: Part 11 scope is inferred rather than approved
risks.mitigation: Quality and Legal approve intended use, regulated records, predicates, validation boundary, and signature controls before implementation.
risks.trigger: A regulated claim is made without an approved intended-use assessment.

risks.title: Portal or Second-Brain implementation is inaccessible
risks.mitigation: Treat repository and runtime access as a Phase 0 gate; do not duplicate an unverified document or memory stack.
risks.trigger: The implementation cannot be inspected at a pinned revision.

risks.title: Authorization or tenant isolation leaks restricted knowledge
risks.mitigation: Enforce source ACLs and tenant predicates before retrieval, add adversarial leakage tests, and fail closed on policy uncertainty.
risks.trigger: A query returns an object not authorized in its source system.

risks.title: Ledger design creates a new mutable source of truth
risks.mitigation: Limit ledger authority to assertions, provenance, ontology versions, and receipts; preserve explicit authoring return paths.
risks.trigger: A user can edit a source-owned business record only in the ledger.

risks.title: Projection drift produces inconsistent answers
risks.mitigation: Stamp every projection with watermarks and versions; compare checksums; rebuild regularly; display degraded freshness.
risks.trigger: Equivalent queries disagree across projections beyond the approved freshness budget.

risks.title: Connector deletion or ACL events are missed
risks.mitigation: Use delta cursors plus periodic full reconciliation, tombstones, replay, watchdogs, and deny on stale authorization state.
risks.trigger: A deleted or revoked item remains retrievable after the approved propagation window.

risks.title: Ontology evolution breaks historical meaning
risks.mitigation: Use stable identifiers, immutable versions, effective dates, explicit mappings, impact previews, and reversible publication.
risks.trigger: A published term change silently reinterprets historical assertions.

risks.title: Retention or residency is lost in derived stores
risks.mitigation: Minimize extracts, map policy state, regionalize stores, propagate disposition, and preserve non-destructive compliance audit history.
risks.trigger: Derived content survives disposition or crosses an unapproved residency boundary.

risks.title: Semantic retrieval is persuasive but unsupported
risks.mitigation: Require citations, confidence, conflict state, refusal on insufficient evidence, and golden-query evaluation before rollout.
risks.trigger: An answer cannot be traced to authorized source revisions.

gates.title: Phase 0 authorization to build
criteria: Quality, Legal, Security, Microsoft 365, Portal, and department owners approved their boundaries.

gates.title: Ledger integrity
criteria: Restore point objective and recovery point objective are met.

gates.title: Connector authority and access
criteria: Every source has an approved authority and authoring return path.
ACL, deletion, replay, and degraded-state tests pass.

gates.title: Ontology stewardship usability
criteria: Administrators complete proposal through rollback without direct database access.
Impact previews identify affected assertions and projections.

gates.title: Records, privacy, and Part 11 qualification
criteria: Quality and Legal approve validation evidence.
Record copies, audit trails, signatures, retention, holds, residency, and tenant isolation pass.

gates.title: Projection rebuild and retrieval quality
criteria: All projections rebuild from empty state.
Golden retrieval, explainability, duplicate, stale, contradiction, and leakage suites meet approved thresholds.

gates.title: Bounded autonomy and zero-drift dispatch
criteria: Revoked and unregistered actors fail closed.
Human-only decisions cannot be executed by agents.
Mission Control import is idempotent and evidence complete.

gates.title: Pilot and go-live readiness
criteria: Architecture pilot meets approved success thresholds.
Rollback, recovery, monitoring, support, and ownership drills pass.
Department heads and control owners approve cutover.
